text: Give me the executive answer on whether shared services AI should be centralized or federated.
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
Lakeshore Holdings should run shared-services AI on a centralized-core, federated-edge model — not a pure choice between the two. Centralize governance, the AI Governance Registry, semantic definitions, the agent/context platform, and Finance-attested value measurement.
Federate the use-case delivery into the functions that own the process (Treasury, Finance, HR, Legal, IT Ops), with a business process owner accountable for adoption and outcomes. Why this shape for Lakeshore specifically.
Your loaded evidence points to a Value Office whose entire premise is reusable context, governed agents, and Finance-attested outcomes across Treasury, Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement, and IT Ops. That reuse thesis dies under a fully federated model — you get five agent stacks, five governance registries, and no cross-OpCo semantic layer.
8M on liquidity forecasting only realize if the Treasurer and CFO own the process redesign, not a central AI team. The concrete split I'd recommend.
Central (Office of CIO, 70 FTE, $31M budget): AI Governance Registry, model risk tiering, the MuleSoft/Entra/M365 Copilot platform, semantic layer for GL and management reporting, reusable agent patterns, and the value-attestation method with the CFO.
Federated to function: process redesign, human-in-the-loop design, adoption, and KPI ownership — Treasurer for Kyriba, Controller for close/reconciliation, Legal Ops for the 2,400 contract requests and 52-day P90 tail, CHRO and GC as Phase 2 discovery only. Sequencing.
